# Specific deficit of the ON response in visual transmission by targeted disruption of the mGIuR6 gene

Taking advantage of the restricted expression of metabotropic glutamate receptor subtype 6 (mGluR6) in retinal ON bipolar cells, we generated knockout mice lacking mGluR6 expression. The homozygous mutant mice showed a loss of ON responses but unchanged OFF responses to light. The mutant mice displayed no obvious changes in retinal cell organization nor in the projection of optic fibers to the brain. Furthermore, the mGluR6-deficient mice showed visual behavioral responses to light stimulation as examined by shuttle box avoidance behavior experiments using light exposure as a conditioned stimulus. The results demonstrate that mGluR6 is essential in synaptic transmission to the ON bipolar cell and that the OFF response provides an important means for transmitting visual information.

# Sestrin2 inhibits uncoupling protein 1 expression through suppressing reactive oxygen species.

Uncoupling protein 1 (Ucp1), which is localized in the mitochondrial inner membrane of mammalian brown adipose tissue (BAT), generates heat by uncoupling oxidative phosphorylation. Upon cold exposure or nutritional abundance, sympathetic neurons stimulate BAT to express Ucp1 to induce energy dissipation and thermogenesis. Accordingly, increased Ucp1 expression reduces obesity in mice and is correlated with leanness in humans. Despite this significance, there is currently a limited understanding of how Ucp1 expression is physiologically regulated at the molecular level. Here, we describe the involvement of Sestrin2 and reactive oxygen species (ROS) in regulation of Ucp1 expression. Transgenic overexpression of Sestrin2 in adipose tissues inhibited both basal and cold-induced Ucp1 expression in interscapular BAT, culminating in decreased thermogenesis and increased fat accumulation. Endogenous Sestrin2 is also important for suppressing Ucp1 expression because BAT from Sestrin2(-/-) mice exhibited a highly elevated level of Ucp1 expression. The redox-inactive mutant of Sestrin2 was incapable of regulating Ucp1 expression, suggesting that Sestrin2 inhibits Ucp1 expression primarily through reducing ROS accumulation. Consistently, ROS-suppressing antioxidant chemicals, such as butylated hydroxyanisole and N-acetylcysteine, inhibited cold- or cAMP-induced Ucp1 expression as well. p38 M

Using a modified telomeric repeat amplification protocol (TRAP), telomerase activity was detected in crickets, cockroaches, and two Lepidopteran insects, though insect telomeres generally consist of pentanucleotide (TTAGG)n repeats—absent in Diptera and some other species, whose telomeres may be maintained without telomerase. Cricket and cockroach telomerase required dATP, dGTP, and dTTP but not dCTP as substrate; sequence analyses confirmed that (TTAGG)n repeats are synthesized by telomerase. Cockroach telomerase occurred in both somatic cells (fat body, muscle, neural tissues) and germ line (testis), indicating expression is not tissue-specific in adults. High activity appeared in crickets and cockroaches, but none was detected in Bombyx mori tissues or cell cultures, nor in two Drosophila and one Sarcophaga cell line—supporting the theory that Dipteran insects maintain telomeres without telomerase.

Three studies report mouse genetic models. mGluR6 knockout mice, exploiting the receptor's restricted expression in retinal ON bipolar cells, lost ON responses to light while OFF responses remained unchanged; retinal organization and optic fiber projections to the brain were normal, and mutant mice still showed visual behavioral responses in shuttle box avoidance experiments, indicating mGluR6 is essential for synaptic transmission to ON bipolar cells and the OFF pathway carries important visual information. A conditional p75(NTR) allele (p75(NTR-FX)) flanking Exons 4-6, encoding transmembrane and cytoplasmic domains, with loxP sites was validated via neural crest-specific p75(NTR)/Wnt1-Cre and conventional null mutants, both showing abnormal hind limb reflexes and peripheral neuropathy. Nrg1 and ErbB4 signalling cell-autonomously controls development of cortical GABA interneuron connectivity, contradicting the prevailing excitatory-synapse view.

# Detection and distribution patterns of telomerase activity in insects.

Telomeres of most insects consist of pentanucleotide (TTAGG)n repeats, although the repeats are absent in Diptera and some other insect species, where the telomere regions are perhaps maintained without telomerase. To understand various and unusual telomere formation in insects, we have studied the characteristic features of a putative insect telomerase that has not been previously described. Using a modified telomeric repeat amplification protocol (TRAP), we first detected the telomerase activity in crickets, cockroaches and two Lepidopteran insects. The telomerase from crickets and cockroaches required dATP, dGTP and dTTP but not dCTP as a substrate and sequence analyses of the products of TRAP revealed that the (TTAGG)n repeats are synthesized by telomerase. The cockroach telomerase was detected both in somatic (fat body, muscle and neural tissues) and germ line (testis) cells, suggesting that expression of this enzyme is not regulated in a tissue-specific manner at an adult stage. While we detected high levels of telomerase activity in crickets and cockroaches, we could not detect activity in all tissues and cell cultures of the silkworm, Bombyx mori and in two Drosophila and one Sarcophaga cell lines. This supports the theory that Dipteran insects maintain their telomeres without telomerase.

# Nitric oxide synthase generates superoxide and nitric oxide in arginine-depleted cells leading to peroxynitrite-mediated cellular injury.

Besides synthesizing nitric oxide (NO), purified neuronal NO synthase (nNOS) can produce superoxide (.O2-) at lower L-Arg concentrations. By using electron paramagnetic resonance spin-trapping techniques, we monitored NO and .O2- formation in nNOS-transfected human kidney 293 cells. In control transfected cells, the Ca2+ ionophore A23187 triggered NO generation but no .O2- was seen. With cells in L-Arg-free medium, we observed .O2- formation that increased as the cytosolic L-Arg levels decreased, while NO generation declined. .O2- formation was virtually abolished by the specific NOS blocker, N-nitro-L-arginine methyl ester (L-NAME). Nitrotyrosine, a specific nitration product of peroxynitrite, accumulated in L-Arg-depleted cells but not in control cells. Activation by A23187 was cytotoxic to L-Arg-depleted, but not to control cells, with marked lactate dehydrogenase release. The cytotoxicity was largely prevented by either superoxide dismutase or L-NAME. Thus, with reduced L-Arg availability NOS elicits cytotoxicity by generating .O2- and NO that interact to form the potent oxidant peroxynitrite. Regulating arginine levels may provide a therapeutic approach to disorders involving .O2-/NO-mediated cellular injury.

Two studies show non-coding 3'UTRs modulate microRNA function. In mouse breast carcinoma 4T1 cells, the versican 3'UTR antagonizes miR-199a-3p, lowering its levels; miR-199a-3p and miR-144 target cell-cycle regulator Rb1, while miR-144 and miR-136 target PTEN. By binding these miRNAs, the 3'UTR freed Rb1 and PTEN mRNAs for translation, up-regulating both synergistically in vitro and in vivo. Cells transfected with the 3'UTR formed smaller tumors than controls, implicating miRNA degradation in tumorigenesis. Separately, the ~1.7 kb spliced, highly abundant murine cytomegalovirus m169 transcript mediates rapid, mutual degradation of cellular miR-27a/b during lytic infection via a single optimized miRNA binding site in its 3'-UTR. Expressing only the m169 3'-UTR from an adenoviral vector sufficed; degradation involved 3'-tailing and trimming. Three mutant viruses unable to target miR-27a/b lost efficiency in vivo.

Danish general practice study by Rune Aabenhus (University of Copenhagen) characterised antibiotic prescriptions for acute respiratory tract infections via clinical-indication-labeled electronic prescriptions (retrospective registry cohort, July 2012–June 2013). Of 456,532 prescriptions, pneumonia was the most common indication (178,354; 39%), followed by acute tonsillitis (21%) and acute otitis media (19%). Penicillin V accounted for 58%, macrolides 18%, amoxicillin 15%. Second-line agent use rose with age, exceeding 40% in patients >75 years. Women were prescribed antibiotics more often regardless of indication. The first Danish study linking prescriptions to clinical indications, it confirms penicillin V as most-prescribed but finds second-line agents overused. Improved prescribing quality is warranted for pneumonia, otitis media and rhinosinusitis, plus further analysis of out-of-hours clinics.

Simvastatin reduces CD40 expression in an experimental model of early arterialization of saphenous vein grafts (VG). Saphenous vein and internal mammary artery (IMA) samples from sixteen patients without statin therapy underwent pulsatile pressure distension and culture with or without Simvastatin (Merck Sharp & Dohme). CD40 was significantly lower in IMA than in distended and non-distended VG. Pressure distension upregulated CD40 in VG segments after 24 and 48 h. Simvastatin significantly reduced CD40 in both venous and arterial samples (P < 0.001 each); this effect was unaffected by L-NAME but reversed by mevalonic acid. Mean soluble CD40L (sCD40L) in culture supernatants increased over time, indicating the vessel wall—not only platelets—is a source of CD40/sCD40L. Simvastatin modulates endothelial CD40–sCD40L in venous and arterial grafts, suggesting a pharmacological tool to prevent graft failure.

Glioblastoma cells exploit glutamate via Ca2+-permeable AMPA receptors; Ca2+ influx phosphorylates Akt at Ser-473, driving proliferation and motility. Dominant-negative Akt blocked AMPA-receptor-accelerated proliferation/migration, while constitutively active Akt rescued apoptosis caused by converting receptors to Ca2+-impermeable via GluR2 cDNA. This glutamate-AMPA-Akt pathway may underlie anaplasia and invasive growth, offering a therapeutic target.

In mast cells, Ca2+ oscillations with accompanying Ca2+ entry through store-operated CRAC channels triggered gene expression, whereas oscillations without entry did not; increased buffering prevented oscillations but not gene activation. Local Ca2+ influx, not global oscillations, drives gene expression at physiological stimulation.

During LTP, synaptic incorporation of GluR1-containing AMPA receptors is controlled by a PKC phosphorylation site on GluR1.
